catalyst.event: Democratic sweep of House and Senate (2026-11-03) removes the legislative path to repealing the remaining IRA clean-energy credits for the next two years
catalyst.action: do not chase the opening gap; bid the 180.0-187.6 shelf, scale in thirds

thesis: First Solar has been de-rated 42% off its 120-day high largely on the risk that a Republican trifecta repeals what is left of the IRA 45X manufacturing credit, which is a direct per-watt subsidy to its US fabs. A Democratic House and Senate facing a Republican president means no repeal bill can pass for two years, so that specific tail is now legislatively closed rather than merely unlikely.
key_risk: The repeal tail can be re-opened administratively - Treasury guidance and IRS rulemaking on 45X foreign-entity-of-concern and domestic-content tests do not need Congress, and tightening them would cut the credit without a vote.
counter_argument: The move is crowded: FSLR ran 174.40 to 185.90 in the two sessions into the election and ENPH ran 18.6%, so the gridlock read is already partly paid for and today opens on a gap that may be the high of the week.

Pre-market sector reads show renewables leading and hyperscalers falling on AI-oversight fears, i.e. the market is pricing legislative action from this Congress in both directions. Gridlock cuts both ways and no bill passes over a presidential veto, which is why the entry is a pullback to a fetched shelf rather than a chase of the gap.

thesis: This is a downgrade of an existing long whose original thesis has been contradicted, not a recommendation to buy. The 110.0 target needed a housing recovery and the Q3 print went the other way: EPS $1.04 against a $1.13 estimate, a 7.7% miss after beats of 30.8%, 18.3% and 47.2% in the three prior quarters, and analyst bullish share has fallen to 54.5% from 63.6%, the only deteriorating revision trend among anything looked at today. counter_argument: The strongest case for patience is that the Q3 miss was small and wood products are cyclical, so a single miss near the bottom of a housing cycle is exactly when the position should be held rather than sold. Against that: the tape rejected the bounce twice in two sessions from 82.00 and 81.20 to close at 75.00 and 74.81, which is distribution rather than basing.

catalyst.event: Divided government seated by the 2026-11-03 Democratic sweep removes the path to further deficit-financed tax cuts, which is the supply-side pressure on the long end. The 10-year already fell from 4.97% to 4.89% as the results came in
catalyst.action: buy the pullback into 79.90-80.60 where the SMA20 (80.09) and SMA50 (80.46) converge - do not pay 81.11 at the top of a five-week run. Half size on the first fill

thesis: The 10-year at 4.91% sits 103bp above an effective fed funds rate of 3.88% while unemployment has turned up to 4.2% from 4.1%, so the long end is carrying a wide term premium into a softening labour market. The election removes the fiscal tail that premium was partly paying for: neither further Republican tax cuts nor Democratic spending can pass a divided Congress, so the marginal path of Treasury supply flattens for two years, and the 10-year moved from 4.97% to 4.89% on the results.
key_risk: The strongest objection is unanswered rather than rebutted: strategists reading the same result flag 2027 debt-ceiling mechanics under divided government as a reason term premium stays high, and gridlock does nothing about the existing deficit. If the term premium is about the debt stock rather than the flow of new legislation, this trade has no edge.
counter_argument: Treasury yields have no consistent historical pattern around midterms, and inflation, Fed policy and growth remain the actual drivers - several strategists called the result short-term noise rather than a repricing. TLT has also already run 77.14 to 81.11 since 2026-10-07, so the easy part of any rate rally has happened, which is exactly why this is a pullback entry and not a market order.

evidence.detail: Fetched 120-day history: Nov 3 close 81.11, ATR14 0.82 (1.01%), SMA20 80.09, SMA50 80.46, range 76.43-87.79.
